subject: Linguistics
title: Synonymy and Antonymy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Synonymy and Antonymy.

hook.text: 'Big' and 'large' seem interchangeable—but you say 'big sister,' never 'large sister.'

buildup.text: True synonyms—words interchangeable in every context—are almost nonexistent.

discovery.text: Synonyms differ in register, connotation, or collocation: 'purchase' vs 'buy,' 'commence' vs 'start.'

twist.text: Antonyms come in pairs: gradable (hot/cold), complementary (alive/dead), and converse (buy/sell).

climax.text: These semantic relations form networks that organize the entire mental dictionary.

punchline.text: No two words fit every slot the same way.

quiz.question: Why are true synonyms rare?
options: Words differ in connotation, register, or collocation
Synonyms are only found in poetry
